hero.headline: Researchers trace mysterious global power grid frequency drops to synchronized battery backup systems
hero.body:
Researchers at Forschungszentrum Jülich in Germany have solved a years-long mystery that has troubled grid managers worldwide: unexplained frequency drops occurring every 60 seconds simultaneously on power grids across continents. The culprit is battery backup systems, including those in data centers, that check their charge status at precisely the same time every minute due to internet-synchronized clocks.

Director Dirk Witthaut led the investigation after Germany's largest transmission system operator, Tennet Germany, brought the puzzle to his team. The researchers initially suspected hydropower plants, which can cause ultra-low frequency oscillations, but could not explain why the pattern persisted without interruption. They realized that such precise timing required a clock mechanism and began installing more than 80 smart power quality meters around the Jülich campus, which houses battery energy storage systems and data center equipment.

The measurements revealed that transformers attached to battery systems peaked every minute, matching the pattern seen on larger grids. Many stationary batteries, from data center uninterruptible power supplies to grid-scale batteries, check their state of charge every 60 seconds. Because these devices synchronize their clocks via internet connection, they perform this check simultaneously, creating a collective disturbance on the grid. Data from Ireland provided confirmation: as data centers grew to consume 18 percent of the country's electricity by 2022, the minute-by-minute frequency drop on the Irish grid quadrupled from 3 millihertz in 2016 to 12 millihertz in 2021, with some recent drops exceeding 20 millihertz.

The researchers recommend that manufacturers add randomization to battery charging schedules rather than checking state of charge exactly on the minute. While Ireland's 50 hertz grid can withstand swings of 200 millihertz, the added disruption from synchronized battery checks could push grids toward blackout conditions when combined with other loads. The team also detected similar periodic power fluctuations in internet-connected devices ranging from smart ovens to computer clusters, though a recent study found that less than 3 percent of such devices run the latest firmware, complicating efforts to deploy software fixes.

The tower, located in the Saudi capital's financial district, was hit by a missile or drone strike that shattered windows across multiple floors. No casualties were reported.

cards.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang acknowledges affair with alleged Chinese government agent as board launches security investigation
cards.teaser: Jensen Huang sent a company-wide memo apologizing for an extramarital relationship with Alice Huang, described as an AI executive and Chinese government agent.
cards.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang sent a memo to employees acknowledging an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, an AI executive and agent of the Chinese government. In the message, Huang apologized to his family and colleagues, stating he took full responsibility for his actions and the harm caused.

The company's board of directors initiated an independent investigation into national security concerns related to the relationship. Huang said he supports the investigation and will cooperate fully, adding that he remains committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting American national security.

cards.headline: Binance names new CFO days after $6.3 billion crypto hack attributed to North Korean hackers
cards.teaser: Justin Yek will succeed Kaiser Ng, who is leaving after more than five years to pursue a new venture.
cards.body:
Binance has named Justin Yek as chief financial officer just over a week after hackers stole approximately $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency from the exchange on October 29. Yek, a former finance executive at payments firm Airwallex, will succeed Kaiser Ng, who is leaving after more than five years to pursue a new venture. A Binance spokesperson said the leadership transition was planned more than six months ago and had no connection to the cyberattack.

The FBI has attributed the attack to North Korean hackers. Binance has pledged to absorb the losses rather than pass them on to customers and said it had replenished 98 percent of affected token assets as of November 3, with approximately $2.85 billion in stolen assets frozen or intercepted.

cards.teaser: House Republican leaders expect enough GOP defections to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth when Representative Thomas Massie forces a vote this week on his resolution accusing
cards.body:
House Republican leaders expect enough GOP defections to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth when Representative Thomas Massie forces a vote this week on his resolution accusing

The political calculus shifted after Republicans suffered major losses in Tuesday's midterm elections, with defeated and retiring members now more willing to back impeachment against a defense secretary whose support has eroded since the Iran war began. Speaker Mike Johnson had canceled votes and sent lawmakers home early before Election Day to avoid the politically difficult impeachment measure.

hero.headline: Paraguay formally charges ousted president Santiago Peña with breach of trust over Ueno Bank collapse
hero.teaser: Prosecutors have formally charged former President Santiago Peña with breach of trust and administration for personal gain, following his impeachment and arrest over the Ueno Bank collapse that left three million Paraguayans unable to access their savings.
hero.body:
Prosecutors in Paraguay have formally charged former President Santiago Peña with breach of trust and administration for personal gain following his impeachment and arrest over the collapse of Ueno Bank. Peña was impeached and placed under house arrest Friday after lawmakers unanimously voted to remove him from office over the digital bank's demise, which has left more than half of Paraguay's population—an estimated three million depositors—unable to access their savings and pensions. Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in as interim president and will serve until 2028.

The impeachment passed with 44 of 45 senators voting in favor. Peña, who until last year held shares in the company that owned the bank, had offered to step down Thursday. Rather than accept his resignation, senators impeached him and charged him with misconduct, stripping him of the immunity usually granted to former presidents. Senate President Basilio Núñez said Peña was found guilty of dereliction of duty. Peña has denied any wrongdoing, and his defense lawyer Ricardo Preda described the allegations as a reckless accusation that was irresponsible and opportunistic.

The impeachment charges alleged Peña had conflicts of interest, manipulated regulatory oversight, diverted pension funds, and participated in an institutional cover-up involving the central bank. Prosecutor Silvia Margarita Gonzalez Vester had said Peña was due to be questioned Saturday over allegations of breach of trust, influence peddling, and misappropriation of funds. The formal charges now confirm prosecutors are moving forward with criminal prosecution.

The bank's collapse prompted widespread protests particularly in the capital, Asunción. Senator Rafael Filizzola called the situation the biggest corruption scandal in Paraguay's democratic history. In an address to the nation Thursday, Peña said he was sorry and that it was never his intention to betray the trust placed in him. Alliana pledged that citizens affected by the financial collapse would be fully compensated.

cards.headline: Krakow shooter's parents and sister found dead at family home as terrorism charges advance
cards.teaser: Polish prosecutors pursue terrorism charges against the gunman accused of killing six people in a far-right attack in Krakow's Main Market Square.
cards.body:
Police confirmed that three bodies found in the home of the 24-year-old gunman who opened fire Saturday in Krakow, Poland, were his parents and sister, who most likely died from gunshot wounds. The suspect, who survived a shootout with police and remains hospitalized in critical condition, faces terrorism charges for the attack in Main Market Square that killed six people, including a British national and an Austrian woman, according to Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek.

Prosecutors are pursuing a separate murder charge for the three relatives found dead in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyskie, about 90 miles from Krakow. Authorities described the shooter as motivated by far-right and ultranationalistic ideologies. Poland declared two national days of mourning after the midday attack, the country's deadliest shooting in decades.

cards.headline: Train collision near Cairo kills seven, injures more than 125
cards.teaser: One passenger train struck another from behind, causing carriages to derail in Giza province.
cards.body:
At least seven people were killed and more than 125 injured when a passenger train traveling between Giza and Fayoum collided with the back of a Cairo-to-Aswan train in Egypt's Giza province on Sunday, according to the Health Ministry. The collision caused the Aswan-bound train to derail onto a countryside road in the al-Ayyat district, overturning at least six carriages.

President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi directed authorities to conduct an urgent investigation to hold accountable anyone found negligent. More than 70 ambulances transported casualties to nearby hospitals. Witnesses described passengers trapped inside overturned carriages with injuries including head wounds and broken limbs.

cards.headline: Surgeons dining in Krakow described treating shooting victims in street before ambulances arrived
cards.teaser: Two doctors who were having lunch near the Main Market Square when a gunman opened fire on Saturday rushed to provide emergency care to wounded officers and the attacker.
cards.body:
Two surgeons who were having lunch near Krakow's Main Market Square when a gunman opened fire Saturday described rushing to treat victims before ambulances arrived. Professor Michal Pędziwiatr said his colleague used his hand to stop bleeding from a gravely injured police officer, treatment Pędziwiatr said "undoubtedly" saved the officer's life. The doctors treated two wounded officers and the attacker himself.

The shooting killed six people and injured 15. The two officers, who were injured while subduing the gunman, emerged from comas Sunday. Polish prosecutors launched a terror investigation after officials said the 24-year-old Polish attacker was apparently inspired by far-right ideologies.

cards.teaser: The three bodies found at the home of the 25-year-old gunman who killed six people in Krakow's Main Market Square on Saturday have been identified as his father, mother, and sister.
cards.body:
The three bodies found at the home of the 25-year-old gunman who killed six people in Krakow's Main Market Square on Saturday have been identified as his father, mother, and sister.

The 25-year-old Polish man drove into the square shortly before 15:00 local time and began firing at random people from his car, killing four women and two men including a British national before armed officers shot and arrested him within three minutes. A minister said early investigations indicate he was inspired by far-right ideologies and described him as an ultra-nationalist.

hero.headline: Philadelphia boycott of Jewish-owned restaurants draws dueling protests, three arrests
hero.body:
A bicycle demonstration organized to promote a boycott of Jewish-owned restaurants drew roughly 300 pro-Palestinian protesters and 200 counter-protesters to Philadelphia on Sunday, resulting in three arrests as the groups clashed verbally in Rittenhouse Square. Philadelphia police arrested a woman on an assault charge, a man on disorderly conduct, and a 17-year-old on an assault on police charge, according to a police spokesperson. Officers formed lines to keep the opposing groups separated as tensions escalated.

The event was organized by Philly Bike On Your Left, which describes itself as an anti-fascist, anti-Zionist social cycling collective. The group announced plans on Oct. 31 to boycott what it called Zionist establishments in solidarity with Palestinians, naming six restaurants including Mac Mart, K'Far Café, Huda, Goldie, Schlesinger's and Dizengoff. Half are owned by restaurant group CookNSolo, whose Israeli co-owners have publicly supported and fundraised for Israel. The restaurants reported long lines of customers showing support during the demonstration.

The planned boycott drew widespread criticism from Philadelphia Mayor Cherelle Parker, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro and Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday, who condemned it on social media. The Anti-Defamation League called the protest an attempt to intimidate a Jewish community that has faced generations of violence and to hold Jewish businesses responsible for events in the Middle East, describing it as antisemitic. Nonprofit organization JewBelong installed billboards at 14 locations across Philadelphia urging residents to support Jewish-owned businesses.

Philly Bike On Your Left said in a statement that the ride had been grossly misrepresented and that the group stands against racism and oppression including antisemitism. The organization said the event was planned around schedules and rejected implications about its timing, which fell on the eve of the anniversary of Kristallnacht, the 1938 Nazi-organized attacks on Jewish communities in Germany, Austria and Sudetenland.

cards.headline: Wisconsin state trooper detained by ICE released under supervision after intervention by DHS secretary
cards.teaser: A Wisconsin state trooper originally from South Africa was released from federal custody late Friday after being detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement officials at an air
cards.body:
A Wisconsin state trooper originally from South Africa was released from federal custody late Friday after being detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement officials at an air

Carel Aaron Van Der Merwe was released under an order of supervision following intervention by Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, according to his attorney. Van Der Merwe entered the United States in 2019 at age 14 and attended high school in New Mexico, according to attorney Mark Christopher.

cards.headline: Six killed in shooting in Krakow, Poland; British citizen among dead
cards.teaser: A gunman killed six people and injured more than a dozen others in a shooting in central Krakow, Poland, on Saturday afternoon, authorities said. A British citizen was among the fo
cards.body:
A gunman killed six people and injured more than a dozen others in a shooting in central Krakow, Poland, on Saturday afternoon, authorities said. A British citizen was among the fo

A British citizen was among the four women and two men killed when the attacker drove onto Main Market Square, a popular tourist attraction in Poland's second-largest city, and began firing at people. Three of the dead were Polish and two have not been identified.

cards.headline: Arrest made in shooting that killed one during Winston-Salem State University homecoming weekend
cards.teaser: Authorities arrested a 20-year-old man in connection with a shooting that killed one person and injured another during homecoming weekend at Winston-Salem State University in North
cards.body:
Authorities arrested a 20-year-old man in connection with a shooting that killed one person and injured another during homecoming weekend at Winston-Salem State University in North

Ziyaire Antonyo Spinks faces charges of murder, assault with a deadly weapon with intent to kill inflicting serious injury, and felony possession of a firearm on an educational campus, Winston-Salem Police Department said Sunday. The shooting Saturday night killed Peyton Izaia Patterson, 19, and injured Alyssa Janae Ellerbee, 19, who was treated at a hospital and released.

cards.headline: Secret Service arrests man near White House with guns who said voices told him to kill Trump
cards.teaser: The Secret Service arrested a man Thursday night near the White House after officers found him in a parked vehicle with multiple guns and ammunition and he told them he heard voice
cards.body:
The Secret Service arrested a man Thursday night near the White House after officers found him in a parked vehicle with multiple guns and ammunition and he told them he heard voice

Officers approached Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos after observing him acting suspiciously in a parked car, according to a Department of Homeland Security statement. Chrinos described hearing voices instructing him to come to Washington and kill the president, the statement said.

cards.teaser: Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Red Bull's Max Verstappen will start from the back of the grid at Sunday's São Paulo Grand Prix after power-unit changes resulted in penalties for both
cards.body:
Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Red Bull's Max Verstappen will start from the back of the grid at Sunday's São Paulo Grand Prix after power-unit changes resulted in penalties for both

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Mercedes' George Russell will also face grid penalties, with Leclerc dropping 10 places and Russell five. Hamilton initially faced a 10-place penalty for exceeding his power-unit allowance for the season.

hero.headline: President Trump defends Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang after board launches investigation into Chinese intelligence targeting
hero.teaser: President Donald Trump publicly defended Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Sunday, calling him an honorable guy and saying he would bring him on an upcoming Asia trip, hours after the company's board announced an independent investigation following reports that Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence.
hero.body:
Nvidia's board of directors announced Sunday that it is opening an independent investigation following reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort, and hours later President Donald Trump publicly defended Huang, calling him an honorable guy who has done an amazing job for the country. Trump said he would support bringing Huang on his upcoming trip through Asia and when asked by reporters if he wished he had acted on intelligence about Alice Huang, the president said no. The investigation comes after The New York Times and Financial Times reported that Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman the newspapers said had been recruited to spy for China. The two are not related.

A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside counsel, will oversee the investigation, which Nvidia said will examine whether national security or company secrets were compromised. The company stated it has no reason to believe either was compromised but called national and economic security paramount to its interests. A person familiar with the matter told NBC News that U.S. intelligence agencies had determined that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy and had a relationship with Nvidia's Jensen Huang.

In a memo to employees that Nvidia shared publicly, Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife. The Financial Times reported that the U.S. government believed Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, whose Singapore-based company was buying Nvidia's advanced chips. U.S. intelligence agencies found she had been recruited by China's top intelligence agency, according to the reports. The New York Times reported that concerns inside the U.S. government about Alice Huang and Jensen Huang rose as high as Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

Nvidia has been at the center of the artificial intelligence boom, producing the world's most sought-after chips. Its top-tier products are mostly restricted from sale to China due to national security concerns, while China has set a 2030 deadline to surpass American AI capabilities. Nvidia is the world's second-largest publicly traded company, worth nearly $4.5 trillion as of Friday.

Before Sunday's announcement, congressional Republicans had already requested a briefing from Huang. Representative John Moolenaar, chairman of the House Select Committee on China, said the reports raise significant national security concerns regarding China's access to sensitive U.S. technology and information. A Nvidia spokesperson said the news would not slow the company and that Huang is committed to continuing as CEO without interruption.

cards.body:
Investors prepare for U.S. inflation figures and results from Constellation Energy, CoreWeave, Nebius, Applied Materials, and Cisco as technology stocks face pressure.

Investors are preparing for a busy week on Wall Street, with earnings from five closely watched companies, fresh U.S. inflation data, and shifting interest rate expectations likely to shape market sentiment.

cards.headline: Warren Buffett's Market-Crash Strategy: Buy and Hold Through Volatility
cards.teaser: The Berkshire Hathaway chairman advises investors to avoid buying only when comfortable and selling when fearful, a strategy that has proven successful through major downturns.
cards.body:
Warren Buffett advises investors to survive market crashes by holding stocks through volatility rather than buying during comfort and selling during fear. The strategy has historically proven effective even through severe downturns, according to market data cited by the investor.

The S&P 500 fell nearly 50 percent during the 2000 dot-com collapse and took until 2007 to reach a new high, yet still delivered total returns exceeding 224 percent between 2000 and 2020. That period included two of the worst U.S. recessions, demonstrating the index's long-term recovery pattern despite short-term losses.

cards.body:
Wall Street reversed from celebration to selloff within 24 hours this week after midterm election results, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite entering correction territory amid c

The Dow surged more than 1,500 points Wednesday following a Democratic sweep of both chambers of Congress, while the S&P 500 rallied nearly 2 percent. By Thursday, stocks had reversed course as investors sold AI and chip stocks.

cards.headline: Musk says SpaceX could acquire legacy telecom carrier and use spectrum ten times more effectively
cards.teaser: Elon Musk told investors on November 6 that SpaceX could acquire a legacy telecommunications carrier and use its airwaves ten times more effectively than current operators, though
cards.body:
Elon Musk told investors on November 6 that SpaceX could acquire a legacy telecommunications carrier and use its airwaves ten times more effectively than current operators, though

Musk made the comments by video at the Baron Investment Conference in New York, adding that any purchase would be conditional on SpaceX using spectrum better than the incumbent. Verizon and AT&T each declined 0.89 percent following the remarks, while SpaceX rose 8.62 percent to $134.27.

cards.headline: Apple accelerates Siri upgrades under internal pressure to match OpenAI and Meta AI assistants
cards.teaser: CEO John Ternus is pushing to expand Siri's capabilities with deeper app control and third-party integrations.
cards.body:
Apple is accelerating its Siri development roadmap as CEO John Ternus pressures software chief Craig Federighi to deliver features that can compete with OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse assistants. The company plans to give Siri fine-grained control over first-party apps, such as cropping images in Photos and organizing Safari tabs, in an update expected with iOS 27.3.

A larger upgrade enabling third-party app integration is planned for spring, allowing Siri to perform tasks like placing food orders through Grubhub or booking restaurant reservations through OpenTable. Apple aims to make Siri more agentic, capable of tracking goals and pursuing ongoing objectives without user intervention for each step, according to Bloomberg.

cards.headline: Elvis Presley estate and Eminem publisher sue AI music company Suno over voice cloning
cards.teaser: The lawsuits claim Suno illegally generates music mimicking the artists and cite Tennessee's ELVIS Act.
cards.body:
Rights holders for Elvis Presley's music and the publisher of Eminem records filed lawsuits against AI music company Suno, alleging it illegally generates music and lyrics that mimic those artists. The Presley suit invokes Tennessee's Ensuring Likeness Voice and Image Security Act, which prohibits AI companies from cloning a singer's voice without permission.

Suno spokesperson Cat McCormack said the company exists to help people create original music and prohibits unauthorized use of artists' work, adding that it blocks prompts for specific artist names and screens uploaded content. The company faces additional lawsuits from Sony, Universal Music Group, and other rights holders over similar claims.

cards.headline: Epic Games confirms launcher support for SteamOS and other Linux distributions
cards.teaser: The company plans to support multiple Linux platforms, but anti-cheat compatibility issues mean Fortnite may not run on Steam Deck.
cards.body:
Epic Games confirmed that its launcher will officially support SteamOS and other Linux distributions, including Fedora, Cachy, and Omarchy, according to Communications Director Jake Jones. The company said it is testing packaging formats and plans to restore AppImage support this month.

The launcher support does not guarantee that Fortnite will run on SteamOS. Epic said Steam Deck does not support the required features for its Easy Anti-Cheat v2 solution, though the company is in discussions with Valve about future compatibility.

cards.headline: Akai opens GitHub repository for MPC music production hardware
cards.teaser: The company has published open-source components for its MPC lineup, enabling developers to modify the devices.
cards.body:
Akai has published an official GitHub repository containing open-source components for its MPC music production hardware, managed by Pete Goodliffe, chief technical officer of the MPC platform. The repository covers three device generations, including the MPC X, MPC Live series, MPC One series, MPC Key models, and the upcoming MPC Sample.

The move does not open-source the entire MPC operating system but provides the Linux environment components required by open-source licenses. Akai previously announced plans to make its MPC Sample hardware sampler open source and is set to unveil 22 new products at NAMM 2027, many available for experimentation.

cards.headline: Sequoia Capital partners blindsided by Roelof Botha's SpaceX board appointment
cards.teaser: Former leader joined board without firm approval, complicating trading of $20 billion stake.
cards.body:
Sequoia Capital partners were reportedly blindsided when former steward Roelof Botha joined the SpaceX board this summer without seeking compliance approval or partnership sign-off, according to the Financial Times. Botha, who stepped down as the firm's leader last year, previously worked with SpaceX CEO Elon Musk at PayPal.

Botha's board role could complicate Sequoia's ability to trade its $20 billion stake in SpaceX. The episode has deepened tensions between Botha and the firm, which this week announced major structural changes including closing its London office and merging early-stage and growth teams. A Sequoia spokesperson said the firm continues to collaborate closely with Botha.

hero.headline: Kenneth Walker scores three touchdowns as Chiefs defeat Jets 35-12, Mahomes plays through elbow injury
hero.body:
Kenneth Walker scored three touchdowns as the Kansas City Chiefs defeated the New York Jets 35-12 on Sunday, snapping a two-game losing streak. Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes threw for 242 yards and two touchdowns despite playing through a right elbow injury sustained on a second-quarter strip-sack by Jets defensive lineman David Bailey that left his arm bent at an awkward angle. Mahomes flexed his elbow on the sideline, threw warmup passes, and returned to the game, though he received treatment from Chiefs trainer Julie Frymyer at halftime and planned additional testing afterward.

Walker finished with 143 yards from scrimmage, including two touchdown receptions and a rushing score, while the Chiefs defense sacked Jets quarterback Geno Smith five times and held New York out of the end zone. The Jets managed just 229 total yards and were credited with minus-9 yards in the third quarter, when Kansas City scored twice to turn a 14-12 halftime lead into a comfortable victory. Smith finished with 165 yards passing for the Jets, who have now lost four consecutive games.

The Jets were without star receiver Garrett Wilson due to a concussion and relied on short passes and runs by Braelon Allen and Breece Hall, who returned from a five-game absence due to a quadriceps injury. Kicker Jason Sanders made four first-half field goals but missed from 53 yards before halftime, as New York failed to reach the end zone.

Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker missed field goal attempts from both 56 yards and on a retry, raising questions about his roster status after Kansas City recently signed former All-Pro kicker Justin Tucker to the practice squad. Coach Andy Reid declined to address the kicking situation, saying he would not make any decisions immediately. The Chiefs improved to 6-2 while the Jets fell to 2-7.

cards.headline: Broncos beat Panthers 26-21 for fifth straight win, extend one-score streak to 16
cards.teaser: Bo Nix threw for two touchdowns as Denver improved to 7-2 and took sole possession of first place in the AFC West.
cards.body:
Bo Nix threw for 237 yards and two touchdowns as the Denver Broncos defeated the Carolina Panthers 26-21 on Sunday for their fifth consecutive win. The victory extended Denver's streak of one-score wins to 16 games and moved the Broncos to 7-2, putting them alone atop the AFC West entering their bye week.

Nik Bonitto sealed the win with a strip-sack of Bryce Young with 1:24 remaining. Jonah Coleman rushed for 57 yards and a touchdown, while Courtland Sutton and Pat Bryant each caught scoring passes. Young threw for 276 yards and three touchdowns for Carolina, which fell to 3-5 despite rallying late.

cards.headline: Norris wins chaotic Sao Paulo GP as Mercedes clinches constructors' title
cards.teaser: Lando Norris took his first win since August after Kimi Antonelli and George Russell both made critical errors in changing conditions at Interlagos.
cards.body:
Lando Norris won the Sao Paulo Grand Prix after McLaren teammate errors by Mercedes drivers handed him the lead in difficult wet-dry conditions. Starting from pole, Norris lost first place to newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli at the start but regained it when the Italian spun at Turn One on lap 20. George Russell, who had climbed into podium contention, spun exiting the pits and lost significant time.

Max Verstappen finished second after starting 21st due to an engine penalty. Despite the mistakes, Russell and Antonelli finished fourth and fifth, clinching Mercedes' ninth constructors' championship and first since 2021. Norris dominated through a late rain shower to secure his first victory since August's Dutch Grand Prix.

cards.headline: Falkirk rise to third in Scottish Premiership with fifth straight win
cards.teaser: John McGlynn's side has defeated Celtic and Hearts in a week, scoring seven goals combined.
cards.body:
Falkirk climbed to third place in the Scottish Premiership after their fifth consecutive victory, a 5-2 win at Hearts. Manager John McGlynn's side defeated defending champions Celtic and became the first team to beat Hearts at Tynecastle in 19 months, scoring seven goals across the two matches. The turnaround comes a month after Falkirk sat 11th, one point off the bottom of the table.

Jacob Murrell leads the league with seven goals and earned the SPFL player of the month award for October. McGlynn brought in 17 new players over the summer after guiding Falkirk to sixth place last season in their return to the top flight.

cards.headline: NFL trade deadline speculation centers on running backs and defensive stars
cards.teaser: Media outlets propose potential deals involving Derrick Henry, Jonathan Taylor, and other impact players as the league's trade deadline approaches.
cards.body:
Multiple sports outlets have published trade proposals ahead of the NFL trade deadline, highlighting running backs Derrick Henry and Jonathan Taylor along with safety Budda Baker and other notable players. The speculation includes scenarios such as Henry joining the Patriots and Baker moving to the Bills.

The reports represent media analysis of potential roster moves rather than confirmed negotiations. ESPN and CBS Sports both released rankings and proposed deals involving players including Tony Pollard, Riq Woolen, and Garrett Wilson as teams evaluate roster adjustments before the deadline.

cards.headline: Norris earns top marks in Sao Paulo Grand Prix driver ratings after pole-to-win performance
cards.teaser: McLaren's Lando Norris received a perfect 10/10 rating for his Brazilian weekend, while Max Verstappen earned 9.5/10 for charging from 21st to second.
cards.body:
Lando Norris received a perfect 10/10 rating for his Sao Paulo Grand Prix weekend, which included pole position in wet conditions and a controlled drive to his third win of the season. The McLaren driver briefly lost the lead at the start but regained control after newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli spun following an early tire change.

Max Verstappen earned a 9.5/10 for his recovery drive from 21st on the grid to second place, making up 10 positions almost immediately in difficult conditions. Red Bull teammate Isack Hadjar received a 9/10 for qualifying well and finishing third despite a few mistakes during the race.

cards.headline: Chelsea among clubs tracking Aston Villa's Kamara
cards.teaser: Chelsea, Inter Milan, and Al-Hilal have placed France midfielder Boubacar Kamara on their watchlists following his injury return.
cards.body:
Chelsea, Inter Milan, and Al-Hilal have placed Aston Villa midfielder Boubacar Kamara on their summer watchlists following the 26-year-old France international's return from injury, according to reports. The development suggests multiple clubs are monitoring Kamara's fitness and form.

Separately, Liverpool and on-loan defender Ronald Araujo plan to wait until season's end before deciding on a permanent transfer from Barcelona for £47 million. Manchester United could pursue Nottingham Forest center-back Murillo with a major summer offer for the 24-year-old Brazil international.

hero.headline: Denis Villeneuve says he is finishing Dune: Part Three while beginning James Bond movie, teases casting before joking at LACMA gala
hero.body:
Director Denis Villeneuve said Saturday that he is putting final touches on the 70mm Imax print of Dune: Part Three while simultaneously starting work on his James Bond film. Speaking at the LACMA Art and Film Gala in Los Angeles, where he was honored, Villeneuve called the third Dune installment a very personal project and the completion of 10 years of work in the desert.

Villeneuve declined to comment on Bond casting speculation on the red carpet, saying every word would be scrutinized, but added that he is having a great time. News broke Friday that Villeneuve and producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman are nearing selection of the new 007, with finalists reportedly including Robert Pattinson, Nicholas Hoult, Callum Turner, Josh O'Connor and Jack Lowden. Inside the gala, Villeneuve began what appeared to be an announcement of the new Bond actor before stopping mid-sentence, joking that producer Amy Pascal was about to have a heart attack.

Actress Nicole Kidman presented Villeneuve with his honor after traveling 15 hours overnight from Australia. Kidman, who has not worked with the director, said she feels she knows the deepest parts of Villeneuve through his films. Actress Anya Taylor-Joy, who appears in Dune: Part Three, said she is excited to see what Villeneuve does with fight sequences in the Bond film, adding that she has worked with four of the five reported finalists.

In his acceptance speech, Villeneuve said Dune: Part Three centers on characters fighting to give their children a better world. He reflected on the importance of human beings continuing to make art together rather than relying on artificial intelligence tools, calling the filmmaking process more important than the result. Dune: Part Three is scheduled to open in theaters in December.

cards.headline: Erika Kirk condemns Dave Chappelle, other comedians for joking about husband's killing
cards.teaser: The widow of conservative activist Charlie Kirk criticized comedians and commentators for using her husband's death as entertainment.
cards.body:
The widow of conservative activist Charlie Kirk criticized comedians and commentators for using her husband's death as entertainment.

Erika Kirk publicly condemned comedians including Dave Chappelle for joking about the killing of her husband, conservative activist Charlie Kirk. In a statement posted on social media Sunday, she called it "beyond disgusting" to see comedians and commentators laugh about political assassination, saying her family will live with the loss every day.

cards.headline: Maya Jama steps down as Love Island host after three years
cards.teaser: The presenter announced on Instagram that it was time to pursue new opportunities after hosting nine seasons of the reality show.
cards.body:
Maya Jama announced she is stepping down as host of Love Island after three years and nine seasons. The 32-year-old presenter wrote on Instagram that it was "time to throw myself into something new," adding that she has "always believed that to truly grow, you have to take a leap every now and then."

Jama took over as host of the reality show in 2023, replacing Laura Whitmore. An ITV spokesperson thanked Jama for her contributions and wished her continued success. Her announcement followed an appearance on Celebrity Traitors that generated speculation about future opportunities.

cards.headline: Ron Howard's 'Avedon' Documentary Examines Photographer's Career and Influence
cards.teaser: The film explores how Richard Avedon changed photography by creating intimate, direct portraits stripped of artifice.
cards.body:
Ron Howard's documentary about photographer Richard Avedon traces how the artist developed his distinctive style of head-on portraits against white backgrounds. The approach originated during World War II when Avedon, stationed in the Merchant Marines at 19, photographed military personnel for identification cards and noticed how the simple format revealed individual character.

The film includes archival clips and interviews with models, critics, and art-world figures including Tina Brown, Twiggy, and Avedon's son John. It examines his work across fashion, portraiture, and commercial photography from 1944 until his death in 2004, documenting roughly 16,000 sittings. The documentary shows how Avedon used minimal setups and brief shooting sessions to capture unguarded moments, producing iconic images of subjects including Marilyn Monroe and Charlie Chaplin.

cards.headline: 'Spy x Family' Confirmed for Season 4 and New Theatrical Film in 2027
cards.teaser: Japanese studio Toho announced a fourth season of the popular anime series and a new feature film, both set for 2027 release.
cards.body:
Japanese studio Toho Co., Ltd. announced that the anime series "Spy x Family" will return for a fourth season in 2027, with a new theatrical film opening in Japan the same year. The studio released a teaser image showing the Forger family—Loid, Yor, Anya, and Bond—walking down a European-style city street.

The series, adapted from the manga by Endo Tatsuya, first aired in 2022 and follows a spy who assembles a fake family for a classified mission, unaware his wife is an assassin and his adopted daughter can read minds. Toho said release dates and story details for both the season and film would be announced later.

cards.headline: Casting predictions spotlight disability drama 'Being Heumann' and Spanish epic 'La Bola Negra' as Oscar contenders
cards.teaser: Two films stand out in the second-year category for their bold discoveries, including 20-plus disabled actors and Spanish pop singer debut.
cards.body:
Awards forecasters are highlighting "Being Heumann" and "La Bola Negra" as leading contenders in the Oscars' second-year casting category. Siân Heder's Apple drama about disability rights activist Judy Heumann featured more than 20 disabled actors, many with little or no acting experience, around breakout Ruth Madeley. 

The Netflix film from Los Javis cast Spanish pop singer Guitarricadelafuente in his acting debut alongside newcomers Milo Quifes and Carlos González, supported by Penélope Cruz and Glenn Close. The 99th Oscars will take place March 14, 2027.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift and Karlie Kloss appear together at Chiefs game for first time in years
cards.teaser: The pair attended Sunday's Kansas City Chiefs-New York Jets game at Arrowhead Stadium, marking their first public appearance together in years.
cards.body:
Taylor Swift and Karlie Kloss attended the Kansas City Chiefs-New York Jets game at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, marking their first public appearance together in years. Cameras captured the model and singer sitting in a box at the Kansas City stadium, accompanied by Swift's parents, Andrea and Scott.

Kloss previously attended Swift's July wedding to Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce at Madison Square Garden. The two became close friends in the early 2010s and appeared on a 2015 Vogue cover together. Kloss was featured in Swift's "Bad Blood" music video that same year.

hero.headline: DeSantis positions for 2028 presidential run as Rubio deflects speculation following GOP midterm losses
hero.body:
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis is positioning himself for a 2028 presidential campaign while Secretary of State Marco Rubio has dismissed reports he is considering a White House bid, as Republicans reassess the party's presidential landscape following midterm election losses. The maneuvering by both Florida Republicans underscores volatility in the early stages of the 2028 primary, where Vice President Vance had been viewed as a likely frontrunner before Tuesday's election results.

DeSantis, whose term as governor ends in January, has fueled speculation through a postelection media campaign that included appearances on podcasts and CNN. Asked whether he plans to run for president, DeSantis declined to answer directly but said the midterm results should serve as a warning to Republicans. "We really got blasted into oblivion, and Florida is kind of the last one standing," he said, emphasizing that Florida was the only red-wall state to withstand the national Democratic gains. He said he has not made plans because "this is a very uncertain time."

Rubio, who serves in the Trump administration until January 2029, has repeatedly said he will not run for president and would not challenge Vance. During the White House election watch party Tuesday, supporters urged Rubio to reconsider running, according to a source familiar with the scene, with some arguing he could restore Republican standing with Latino voters. Two days later, published reports suggested Rubio was actively considering resigning to pursue a presidential campaign. Rubio denied the reports to the New York Times, and longtime associates told Axios the reporting was false.

Both DeSantis and Rubio previously ran for president, in 2024 and 2016 respectively, giving them national profiles. Some Republican donors have indicated they would support DeSantis in 2028, and at least one supporter has told Vance he should not run, according to the Wall Street Journal.

cards.headline: House Republicans weigh impeaching Defense Secretary Hegseth this week over alleged illegal continuation of Iran war
cards.teaser: House Republican leaders expect enough GOP defections to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth when Representative Thomas Massie forces a vote this week on his resolution accusing
cards.body:
House Republican leaders expect enough GOP defections to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth when Representative Thomas Massie forces a vote this week on his resolution accusing

The political calculus shifted after Republicans suffered major losses in Tuesday's midterm elections, with defeated and retiring members now more willing to back impeachment against a defense secretary whose support has eroded since the Iran war began. Speaker Mike Johnson had canceled votes and sent lawmakers home early before Election Day to avoid the politically difficult impeachment measure.

cards.headline: Attorney General dismisses Calley Means' White House corruption allegations as former FDA chief backs some claims
cards.teaser: Attorney General Todd Blanche on Sunday dismissed corruption allegations made by former Trump health adviser Calley Means against senior White House officials, calling Means a disg
cards.body:
Attorney General Todd Blanche on Sunday dismissed corruption allegations made by former Trump health adviser Calley Means against senior White House officials, calling Means a disg

Blanche told CNN he would not investigate claims Means made on a podcast, even as former FDA Commissioner Marty Makary corroborated aspects of the allegations and Representative Marlin Stutzman, an Indiana Republican, said any impropriety claims should be examined. Means alleged in a Friday interview that former White House chief of staff Susie Wiles blocked an initiative to examine children's sugar consumption because she wanted sugar industry donations for midterm elections.

cards.headline: Trump replaces chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller after GOP midterm losses
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump announced Friday that he is replacing Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff with longtime adviser Stephen Miller, following Republican losses in Tuesday'
cards.body:
President Donald Trump announced Friday that he is replacing Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff with longtime adviser Stephen Miller, following Republican losses in Tuesday'

Wiles submitted her resignation Thursday night after Trump blamed her for the election results in which Republicans lost control of Congress. Trump will install Miller, currently deputy chief of staff, in the position starting Monday.
